newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades mostly sideways.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades mostly sideways.

text.p: German call money traded mostly sideways on Tuesday as liquidity conditions were said to be in equilibrium and few new factors affected trade.
Overnight funds traded between 3.08/10 percent on Tuesday after 3.05/10 percent on Monday.

Dealers said the liquidity position was largely in equilibrium with conditions mostly normalised at the beginning of the month. Consequently dealers expected the Bundesbank would keep the amount of liquidity steady this week, replacing the 72.9 billion mark repo pact which expires on Wednesday. "There is no need for a big add or drain," a dealer said.
But in light of the relatively strong liquidity position, another dealer said that a small drain in funds could be possible.

Banks held 43.6 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank on Monday, down from 43.9 billion marks on Friday. But the monthly average for holdings rose to 43.8 billion marks compared with 41 billion marks.
Banks' Lombard borrowings were negligible on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.11100 percent on Tuesday compared with 3.13167 percent on Monday.
